title: Two sides and a ball: score in the other side's goal
summary: One ball, two ends, a goal behind each end, first to N points. Covers pong, air hockey, table football, a penalty duel: anything where a ball crossing a line is a point.
applies_when: two sides (player against AI, or two AIs) defend opposite ends of one bounded court
a point is a ball or puck crossing a line or entering a goal
the player's piece moves on a rail or inside its own half and returns the ball by contact
not_when: players run freely with the ball and pass it (needs possession and team AI the seed does not show)
there is no opponent and the goal is a time or lap count: use card.timed_drive or card.knock_down

data_files.role: the venue as one tl.layout/1 file: floor, walls, the ball and both paddles as props with ids, scenery, cameras
the whole rule set: the two sides and the score that wins
every number a designer turns: serve and top speed, angles, paddle speed, the rival's speed (the difficulty)

do: Put the ball and both movers in the layout as kit props with ids; let the kernel make their bodies (TLBall.create with the part, TLBodies.from_part with axis locks).
Make each goal a trigger behind the defender that only sees the ball's group; in its signal handler set a flag and score in _pack_tick.
Choose the floor surface for the feel you want: the law table decides how the ball slides (ice keeps it fast; concrete stops it).
Give the AI intents (where the ball will be, how hard to go there) through TLSteer; make difficulty one tuning number: the rival's speed.
Serve with seeded randomness (ctx.pick for the side, ctx.rng for the angle) and add a dead-ball rule that re-serves a ball that stopped.
Raise the ball speed a little on every return so a rally always ends.
dont: Do not build walls, goals or the floor from script boxes when a kit part exists (barrier_wall, goal, rink, ground_patch).
Do not write score or win logic in the script: sides and score_to_win in rules.json already are the rules.
Do not move the paddle by setting its position: drive it with a velocity so it still collides.
Do not create, free or move bodies inside a trigger or contact signal handler.
Do not make the rival as fast as the player: an unbeatable AI is a bot that never finishes.

bot.plays_by: the player's own actions only: it predicts where the ball crosses its line (mirrored at the side walls) and offers the paddle edge that sends the ball away from the rival.
bot.wins_when: the rules say state over, winner player, reason score, the player's score equals score_to_win and the HUD shows the win text.

acceptance: The bot wins by score at seeds 1, 2 and 3 inside the default bot frame budget.
A do-nothing player loses: the rival scores when nobody defends.
No rally lasts forever: ball speed grows per return or the dead-ball rule fires.
Lint reports 0 bypasses and 0 kit parts added.
Both registered cameras show the whole court and both scores are on the HUD.

variants.ask: air hockey or ice hockey shoot-out
variants.change: swap ball for puck and the court for a rink (its goals are child parts with tl_mouth for the goal trigger); keep planar on.
a second TLBall in the same group; the goal triggers already count it.
the rival's speed and the ball's max_speed in tuning.json; nothing else.
the floor's surface in the layout (ice, concrete, wood): friction and bounce follow from the law table.
